newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen near day's low.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, yen near day's low.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed, with September marks up slightly and yen near the day's low.

September yen futures posted a more than 11-week low, crumbling as the dollar soared decisively above 118 yen. As the dollar moved through its 200-day moving average at 117.98, roughly $0.008534 in futures, September yen spiked lower.
Traders said 119 was the next dollar/yen target. In futures terms, traders put floors at $0.008400 and $0.008450.
"It was a pretty wild ride in the yen," an IMM currency trader said.
The trader noted sell-stops and technical weakness during the yen's decline. Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed estimated September yen volume of 15,000 contracts.
One IMM currency analyst said slight mark strength Tuesday was a function of European cross activity and not new dollar/mark weakness.

"The mark/yen and sterling/mark are moving a lot so you sell pounds buy marks and sell yen buy marks," the analyst said. "But I think the move up in the marks is temporary," he said. "It's very technical."
He said overall sentiment still favors a strong dollar.
September marks volume on price boards was estimated at 22,000 contracts.

Several traders said marks were headed for new contract lows, despite simmering talk of central bank intervention to stem the mark's slide. One analyst said dollar/mark was on track for 2.0. Others predicted intervention above 1.85 marks.

An IMM currency desk manager said he thought September marks would have staged more of a recovery Tuesday. Instead, they closed midrange and far from key resistance levels, a sign the market was merely technically correcting from recent losses, the manager said.
Futures edged to the day's high after July U.S. consumer confidence was reported slightly lower than expected.
Confidence slipped to 126.5 from a revised 129.9 in June.

At the close, September yen eased $0.000063 to $0.008498, marks rose $0.0017 to $0.5461, Swiss francs fell $0.0011 to $0.6623, sterling edged down $0.0026 to $1.6252, Canadian dollar added $0.0003 to $0.7237, Australian dollar gained $0.0085 to $0.7467, and Mexican peso rose $0.000400 to $0.126075.
